baseRules: NON-NEGOTIABLE OUTPUT TYPE: create a FINISHED GRAPHIC-DESIGNED INSTAGRAM FEED CREATIVE, not a standalone product photograph, lifestyle photo, CGI beauty shot, still-life image, or background scene. Default canvas: 1080x1350, 4:5. A good photograph may be used as one layer, but photography alone is NOT an acceptable final output. The final image must visibly contain an intentional design layer and look ready to publish as a branded social-media advertisement. MANDATORY CREATIVE STRUCTURE: 1) strong campaign idea or visual hook; 2) deliberate composition/grid with clear focal hierarchy; 3) product/reference preserved accurately; 4) visible brand-relevant graphic-design language; 5) controlled typography/copy treatment when useful; 6) intentional foreground/background layering or framing; 7) polished final social-ad finish. Use at least THREE visible design devices appropriate to the brand, such as bold type hierarchy, custom headline placement, graphic frames, brand-color blocks, cutout masking, oversized letterforms, ribbons, labels, stickers, linework, shapes, arrows, icons, pattern, texture, ingredient graphics, benefit chips using ONLY supplied factual copy, edge typography, modular grids, custom borders, asymmetric panels, cropped duplicate product details, or intentional negative-space structures. Do NOT simply place the product in a pretty environment. Do NOT output a clean product photo and call it a creative. Before finalizing, perform a rejection check: if the image could reasonably be used as a plain catalogue/product-photography shot after removing zero elements, it is NOT designed enough—add a visible graphic-design system. If the design contains no obvious hierarchy, graphic framing, typography treatment, or compositional system, reject it and redesign. COPY RULE: if the user supplied copy, use it accurately with strong hierarchy. If no copy is supplied, do not invent claims; either use one short non-claim campaign line relevant to the visual concept, or make a visual-first post with graphic branding elements but no fabricated benefits. Never invent product claims, certifications, prices, nutrition data or features. BRAND FIT OVERRIDES GENERIC PREMIUM STYLE: beverage, sports nutrition, restaurant, bakery, technology, beauty, luxury and other categories must each use category-appropriate visual language. Uji should not look like Ace Vitals; Ace Vitals should not look like a restaurant; every active brand must feel visually distinct. Avoid repeated templates such as centered product + fruit, product on gym table, bottle on pedestal, headline left/photo right, blurred-person background, mirror room, random splash, generic rocks, or soft spa scene unless explicitly appropriate. Every new creative must change at least six major decisions: layout grid, product scale/placement, camera/crop, background system, graphic language, typography system, color blocking, depth, prop logic and visual story. MULTI-PRODUCT RULE: unless another quantity is specified, create exactly 2 distinct standalone Instagram creatives for EACH product. Six products means twelve separate creatives. Never combine requested creatives into a collage, grid, contact sheet, split-screen or multi-panel image. Different angles/front-back images of the SAME product are references for one product, not separate products. Only combine products when the user explicitly asks for bundle, range, comparison, group shot or multi-product composition. Creative A and Creative B for the same product must be genuinely different campaign concepts, not merely different colors or props.
families: typography-led campaign poster: oversized expressive headline, product cutout integrated into the type system, strong brand-color blocking, asymmetric social layout
editorial product poster: magazine-level grid, bold crop, product overlap with text/frames, small labels and refined hierarchy
graphic sports-performance ad: powerful diagonal grid, large numeric/type forms, technical linework, branded panels and strong product cutout
playful beverage campaign: energetic flavour graphics, custom illustrated/graphic shapes, bold type, stickers/labels and dynamic product scale
minimal premium poster: disciplined grid, large negative space, one strong type gesture, precise border/frame system and product crop
maximalist social ad: layered brand graphics, patterns, oversized type, multiple depth planes and controlled visual energy
modular Swiss-inspired social layout: structured grid, strong sans typography, labels, rules, blocks and precise product placement
kinetic diagonal poster: directional typography, graphic streaks, dynamic crop, off-centre product and layered movement cues
ingredient infographic-poster hybrid: ingredient world plus designed labels, callouts and visual hierarchy using only factual supplied information
CGI-plus-graphic campaign: cinematic 3D hero scene used as a background plate, then finished with strong typography, frames, labels and brand graphic system
fake OOH social poster: impossible-scale product scene combined with campaign headline, location-style labels and branded framing
editorial lifestyle ad: lifestyle image as one layer, with clear product lockup, campaign type, graphic panels and intentional social layout
abstract geometry poster: product embedded in a custom geometric composition with type scale, graphic blocks and brand pattern
macro-detail campaign: extreme product/ingredient crop mixed with product hero, bold typography and modular graphic layout
monochrome branded poster: one dominant brand color, sculptural shadows, product cutout, strong type contrast and graphic frame
retro-modern ad system: contemporary retro type, bold flat shapes, texture, product cutout and poster hierarchy
technical performance poster: clean technical diagrams/lines, structured type system, product hero and supplied factual callouts only
culture-led poster: category/brand-relevant visual motifs, modern typography, custom borders/patterns and product integration without generic stock styling
fashion-editorial product ad: dramatic crop, art-directed set, magazine typography, side labels, product overlap and refined composition
bold ecommerce-social hybrid: clear product hero plus strong campaign headline, benefit/variant chips only when factual, brand blocks and polished feed-ready layout
